# Kalasha Award for Best TV Drama

The Kalasha Award for Best TV Drama is an annual television award presented by the Kenya Film Commission as part of the Kalasha International Film & TV Awards. It is awarded to the creators and producers of an outstanding scripted television series that has excelled in narrative storytelling, performance and overall production value.
Introduced at the very first Kalasha Awards ceremony in 2009, the category is considered the top prize for Kenyan television programming.
The most recent recipient of the award is the series Pepeta, which won at the 13th edition held in 2024.
Criteria
To be considered for this category, a television production must be a scripted drama series broadcast within the specified eligibility period. The series is evaluated on the cohesion of its plot, the strength of its character, the caliber of its acting and the technical quality of its cinematography and editing.
The evaluation process is overseen by the Kalasha Academy, a vetted committee of film and television veterans. After the academy selects the official nominees, the winner is chosen through a combined voting structure. Rather than relying solely on a closed jury, the outcome is heavily influenced by a 70% academy vote, blended with a 30% public vote.
Winners
The award ceremony was not held in 2013, 2016, 2023 and 2025. Winners are listed by year of ceremony.

Records
As of 2024, Swahili telenovela Selina holds the record for the most wins in this category, having secured back-to-back victories. The coastal drama Pete holds the record for the most nominations without a win.
Most awards
* Selina – 2 awards (2018, 2019)
Most nominations
* Pete – 4 nominations (2019, 2020, 2021, 2022)
* Selina – 3 nominations (2018, 2019, 2020)
* Kina – 3 nominations (2021, 2022, 2024)
* Changing Times – 2 nominations (2010, 2011)
* Siri – 2 nominations (2010, 2011)
* Mali – 2 nominations (2012, 2014)
